# Research Methodologies — Open-Set Recognition

Despite the course name, this repo does **not** teach research methods — it *applies* one. It is a
**written literature study on [[open-set-recognition]] culminating in OpenGAN**, produced for the
*Research Methodologies* course (WUST, Electronic Media in Business and Commerce, 2026). 9 files,
31 KB of prose across three markdown documents.

**It is the only two-author repository in the source set.** Wuxi Bao and Alimuzzaman Bhuiyan are
credited jointly in `README.md` §9 and in the `NOTICE` copyright line.

**Status: coursework, finished and frozen at last commit 2026-07-11.** "All finished and frozen"
(interview, 2026-07-28).

## The method it actually used

[[literature-review-synthesis]], not experimentation. No dataset, no code, no sampling frame, no
hypothesis test. The design is: frame the problem → map the method families → deep-dive the
generative family → spotlight one method → compare on benchmarks **taken from the source paper**.
Quality control is a stated provenance boundary rather than reproduction —
[[report-cites-benchmarks-rather-than-reproducing]].

## Content recorded as concepts

[[open-set-recognition]] (closed-set vs open-set, rejection as a valid answer) ·
[[openmax-and-extreme-value-theory]] (Weibull tail fit redistributing softmax mass) ·
[[generative-adversarial-network]] (the minimax objective, Wasserstein loss as the stability
alternative) · [[literature-review-synthesis]] (the method itself).

OpenGAN's two moves are the report's payload: discriminate in **feature space** rather than pixel
space, and select the checkpoint on a small held-out open set. The report is explicit that without
the second move performance is "essentially random".

## Findings

- **Five commits in 16 seconds** on 2026-07-11, in publish order — scaffolding + slides, figure,
  both chapters, the main report, licence + NOTICE. [[import-finished-work-into-git]] in its purest
  form; the work itself has no git trace at all.
- **This is the only repo in the group with no `origin/HEAD` set** — a small tell that the remote
  was created differently from [[computer-project-management]], [[physics-exam-prep]] and
  [[privacy-policy-template]].
- **The provenance boundary is the repo's strongest engineering habit.** `NOTICE`, the inline "not
  experiments run for this coursework" note under the results table, and the licence footer all say
  the same thing three times in three places. See [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].
- **A stated finding the report deliberately keeps in tension with its own conclusion.** The report
  spotlights OpenGAN while also quoting Vaze et al.'s result that "a good closed-set classifier is
  already a good open-set detector" — an argument that a stronger baseline may close much of the
  gap. Both claims are left standing; neither is resolved. Recorded rather than tidied, in the
  spirit of [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]].
